question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-x(t)+2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=0$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[2,\text{ }1]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[-1,\text{ }1]^{T},$ respectively. Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the system?

*Hint: Here, the dotted line represents the equilibrium solutions.*
question.worked_solution:
The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Let's now sketch the phase portrait.

- First, notice that ${x}_{E}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are the equilibrium solutions of the system since ${x}_{E}^{′}(t)=0.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=\frac{1}{2}x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274360/assets/c3b4e48221f7896f6082773552ef009b14ab0cbaf626068040fa4c1b87a71a45.png)

- Now, the line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 
$y=-x$
and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line. Since ${e}^{-3t}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach the origin as $t\to \infty .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274360/assets/307aee5d0083ed352e9f24acb5ed1107f6096b8805810190841317e77a891627.png)

All other non-equilibrium solutions are parallel to the vector ${v}_{2}.$ So, the phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274360/assets/96130e419134ae5825f4ec68987e4c2d54e1ee3521c5cfd2a5f7d1e29bfb0954.png)
